key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, reducing porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak microhardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the spray gas ratio is a practical process lever for optimizing wear- and corrosion-resistant coating quality on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si-based self-fluxing coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied O2/C2H2 ratio across 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97% to 0.90%, roughness from 4.70 to 2.99 µm, adhesion rising from 22.14 to 35.02 MPa, and maximum microhardness of 1051.7 HV at O2/C2H2 = 1.1.
watch_item: The results are process- and material-specific, so the optimal O2/C2H2 ratio may shift with substrate, powder feedstock, torch setup, or coating thickness.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
